source.title: Do LLM Modules Generalize? A Study on Motion Generation for Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Ming-Yi Wang; Jing-Ke Wang; Teng-Ju Ye; Jun-Bo Chen; Kai-Cheng Yu

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in autoregressive motion-generation models, extending the question to autonomous-driving trajectories rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training and validation losses across model sizes and data volumes, so these bear on V5 and on V7's claim that curves can depart from a single power law. It does not fit scaling exponents or test extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, language-model loss scaling, or downstream task predictability. Table 3's accuracy and training-loss results are not included as rows because the relevant measure here is held-out loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains autoregressive next-token motion-generation transformers (0.8M–11.6M parameters) from scratch on Waymo data at 10%, 100% and 800% (augmented) data. It reports held-out validation loss, so it bears on V5 (power-law-like scaling in a non-text modality) and, through the bend at augmented data, on V7. It fits no exponents, makes no extrapolation and runs no compute-optimal sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say performance follows power-law-like scaling within their range, and that larger models help when data is sufficient. However, the gains they cite for model size are mainly in training accuracy. Their own augmented-data validation loss does not improve beyond the Medium or Big model. They attribute this to limited, redundant data and overfitting, and they did not study larger models.
record.recipe_differences: This is an autoregressive motion-generation scaling sweep on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, not a language-model scaling-law experiment. It reports validation losses but does not fit exponents or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling trend varies with data volume and model size; the authors note redundant augmented data and overfitting in the largest model.
record.problems: The scale range is limited to models from 0.8M to 11.6M parameters and data settings of 10%, 100%, and 800% (augmented). The paper does not fit or report scaling exponents, and says the augmented data are redundant and the largest model shows overfitting. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3's training losses and token accuracies are omitted because the claim concerns held-out loss. No other relevant held-out-loss outcomes were reported beyond the listed validation-loss entries.

untested.parts: No power law is fitted. The parameter range is about 14x (0.8M–11.6M), not several orders of magnitude. There are no image or video models and no fine-tuning or transfer scaling. Augmented data is repeated-context data rather than fresh data.
No exponents are fitted. Parameter-counting conventions, schedules and fitting methods are not compared, and no compute-optimal split is estimated.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Sim Agents metrics are not related to scale or loss.

missing.what: Validation loss versus parameter count at fixed data. At 10%: 1.72, 1.65, 1.66, 1.64. At 100%: 1.60, 1.51, 1.50, 1.49. At Aug: 1.52, 1.48, 1.48, 1.49. This shows non-monotone or flat model-size scaling beyond Medium, which the current data-sweep rows do not frame.

record.verdict_notes: The study uses tiny models (≤11.6M parameters) and about 35M tokens, and reports no uncertainty. The 'scaling law' language is qualitative, with no fit. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann but is not an original source. Augmented data uses multiple anchor times over the same scenarios, so it is closer to a repeated-data regime.

versions.untested_parts: The study is about motion-generation models, not language models.
No small-run fits or predictions for larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The study tests motion generation only; it does not test image or video models, repeated data as a training regime in isolation, fine-tuning or transfer, or whether fitted power-law forms match those for text.
No downstream-task performance relationship with pretraining loss or scale is tested.

The study does not estimate exponents, compare fitting methods or parameter-counting conventions, or test compute-optimal allocation. Its evidence concerns data-scale behavior, augmented-data redundancy, and overfitting.

relationships.condition: Genuine data increase 10%→100%, all four model sizes, Waymo motion generation
relationships.reason: Validation loss falls for every model with 10x real data (e.g. 1.72→1.60, 1.64→1.49). Rows R2, R5, R8 and R11.
relationships.display_finding: Tenfold more real data reduced validation loss for every model, including decreases from 1.72 to 1.60 and from 1.64 to 1.49.

relationships.condition: 800% augmented data, and parameter scaling beyond the Medium (3.7M) model
relationships.reason: Augmented 8x data gives small or no loss gains (R3, R6, R9, R12), with the Large model flat at 1.49 and overfitting. Per Table 3 text, at Aug data validation loss is 1.48/1.48/1.49 for Medium, Big and Large, so model-size scaling stalls. No power law is fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Eightfold augmentation yielded little or no loss improvement, with validation losses of 1.48, 1.48, and 1.49 for Medium, Big, and Large, respectively, and overfitting in Large.

relationships.condition: Redundant augmented data at 800%, larger models
relationships.reason: The authors report the 100%→800% trend deviating from ideal scaling, and the loss curve flattens (R6, R9, R12). The curve's shape depends on the diversity of the data.
relationships.display_finding: Expanding augmented data from 100% to 800% flattens loss curves and departs from ideal scaling, linking curve shape to data diversity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
